gap: No result ChatGPT got states that AV Access's own iDock M10 page excludes the MacBook + Windows laptop pairing ("This model is not compatible with a MacBook + Windows laptop setup"): the Mac-friendly AV Access dock is only for a MacBook plus a desktop, and its sibling for two laptops, the iDock C20, mirrors on a Mac.
standout_why: I compared it against the two cited Dock Gear HQ pages (built-in KVM docks, and dual-monitor setups), the cited ThunderboltLaptop dual-monitor page, the cited AV Access 'best KVM switches' guide, and the uncited top results from Tried Tested Reviewed and The Office Journal. Dock Gear HQ describes the M10 as 'one MacBook/laptop… plus one desktop' and lists its base M1/M2 limit. ThunderboltLaptop has the M3 lid-closed caveat, so the chip matrix is partly covered. None of these pages states the maker's explicit exclusion of a MacBook + Windows laptop pair. Tried Tested Reviewed says the M10 is 'Built for MacBook plus Windows PC combo' and 'Not compatible with Mac Mini or Studio', and the maker's FAQ contradicts the second claim. None of the pages mentions the AV Access cap that drops a 5120×1440 super-ultrawide to 3840×1080 on the C20, KD-E10 and M10.
decides: For the most common reading of this question (two laptops on one dock), it confirms the split ChatGPT hinted at. Two Windows laptops: iDock C20. A MacBook plus a Windows laptop with two extended Mac screens: not the M10, which the maker excludes, and not the C20, which mirrors. That leaves a DisplayLink dock such as the StarTech 129N. A MacBook plus a desktop: iDock M10, provided the Mac is M3 with the lid closed, M4, or a Pro/Max chip. Separately, a shopper with a 49-inch 5120×1440 monitor should skip all three AV Access docks, because each caps that panel at 3840×1080.

findings.label: Excluded pairing
findings.value: Not compatible with a MacBook + Windows laptop setup; the second computer is a desktop on HDMI + DP + USB-C inputs labelled '② Desktop'
findings.source_title: iDock M10 KVM Switch Docking Station for MacBook and PC – AV Access
findings.note: Quoted from the maker's page. The same page also has a 'MacBook + Windows PC' tab, which means a desktop PC.

findings.label: Mac chip matrix for two extended displays
findings.value: M1/M2 base: one external display only. M3 base: two extended only with the lid closed (mirror with the lid open). M4/M5 or any Pro/Max: two extended
findings.source_title: iDock M10 KVM Switch Docking Station for MacBook and PC – AV Access
findings.note: The page's FAQ lists 'M1/M2/M3/M4 Pro, M1/M2/M3/M4 Max, and M3/M4' and leaves out M5, so the page is internally inconsistent about M5.

findings.label: Mac ports used
findings.value: 2 USB-C/Thunderbolt ports on the MacBook (dual USB-C to dual USB-C cable, 0.8 m, USB 3.2 Gen 2, included)
findings.source_title: iDock M10 KVM Switch Docking Station for MacBook and PC – AV Access
findings.note: The maker says two ports are 'required on the MacBook for dual extended displays'. 100 W charging to the MacBook from a 20 V/6 A adapter.

findings.label: Mac mini / Mac Studio as the desktop
findings.value: Supported if both Macs have a Pro chip or M3 or newer
findings.source_title: iDock M10 KVM Switch Docking Station for MacBook and PC – AV Access
findings.note: Contradicts triedtestedreviewed.com, which says 'Not compatible with Mac Mini or Studio'.

findings.label: Price, maker US store
findings.source_title: iDock M10 KVM Switch Docking Station for MacBook and PC – AV Access

findings.label: Laptop port requirement and Mac behaviour
findings.value: Each laptop's USB-C port must support DP Alt Mode and DP MST. On macOS, 'any additional monitor will be in mirror mode'
findings.note: The page's Mac FAQ sends Mac users to the iDock M10. Up to 60 W charging per laptop at the same time. 'USB Mode requires the latest firmware.' No clipboard sharing.

findings.label: Super-ultrawide limit
findings.value: 3440×1440 at 60 Hz supported; a 5120×1440 display is limited to 3840×1080
findings.note: The maker's FAQ wording. The same cap appears on the KD-E10 and M10 pages.

findings.label: Price, maker US store
findings.note: The range presumably covers variants or bundles. ChatGPT showed $259.99.

findings.label: Pairing and limits
findings.value: One USB-C laptop (DP MST, 100 W) plus one desktop (DP 1.4a + HDMI 2.0b + USB-B 3.0). macOS mirrors. Gigabit Ethernet goes to the USB-C laptop only. Switching by panel button only. A 5120×1440 display is capped at 3840×1080
findings.note: Quoted: 'MacOS doesn't support USB-C MST… two duplicate contents will be displayed'; 'LAN… (For USB C Laptop only)'. The page also says 'please additionally use your laptop's original adapter' when charging, which leaves it unclear whether a second adapter is required. Price shown: $169.99.

unsourced: Sabrent SB-TB4K host list (Thunderbolt 3/USB4/AMD support) and the number of extended displays on base Apple-silicon Macs: sabrent.com/products/sb-tb4k returned HTTP 429 on three attempts (WebFetch twice, storecheck once). I found no manual or named reviewer within budget.

TESmart HDC202-X24 list of Macs that cannot run dual extended displays on PC1 (a search snippet said it covers base M1/M2/M3 MacBooks and the base M1 Mac mini): tesmart.com product pages returned HTTP 429 on all three attempts, so it is not reported.

StarTech 129N-USBC-KVM-DOCK OS matrix (macOS versions, ChromeOS, Linux), host requirements and per-host charging from the maker: the startech.com product page returned no spec text through WebFetch, and the datasheet PDF was image-only. Rival pages give 90 W active / 45 W inactive and say a DisplayLink driver is required, but I did not confirm this on a maker document.
